name: Pili Gemini

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Trichoscopic Diagnosis of Pili Gemini

criteria.description: Presence of two hair shafts emerging from a single hair follicle
Trichoscopic visualization of bifurcated hair shafts with shared follicular ostium
No evidence of follicular scarring or inflammation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of twin hair shafts from a single follicle confirmed clinically and by trichoscopy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by trichoscopy; histopathology rarely required.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Twin hair shafts emerging from a single follicular opening
searchTerms: twin hair strands from single opening

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bifurcated hair shafts with normal pigmentation
searchTerms: split hair shafts with normal color

common.symptomName: Localized areas of increased hair density
Hair shafts of normal thickness and texture

occasional.symptomName: Mild hair fragility in affected follicles
searchTerms: slightly fragile hair in some follicles

occasional.symptomName: Presence of short, broken hairs adjacent to twin follicles
searchTerms: short broken hairs near twin follicles
broken hair fragments by double follicles
damaged hairs adjacent to twin shafts
excess keratin around twin hair follicles

imaging: Trichoscopy showing twin hair shafts from single follicular ostium
genetic: No known genetic mutations identified; sporadic cases reported
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic twin hair shafts

distinguishingFeatures: Multiple (more than two) hair shafts per follicle
Hair shaft splitting at distal ends
No twin hair shafts emerging from single follicle
Associated with hair shaft damage rather than follicular anomaly

redFlags: Rapid onset of hair shaft abnormalities
Signs of folliculitis or scalp inflammation
references: Tosti A, et al. Trichoscopy of hair shaft abnormalities. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2013.
Harries MJ, et al. Hair shaft disorders: clinical and trichoscopic features. Clin Exp Dermatol. 2010.
